text:
maya: Heads up — since ~10:02 UTC we've seen ~10% of pod->pod requests get `lookup <service>: i/o timeout` in cluster asia-east1. GPU job scheduler retries spike, autoscaler marks nodes as unhealthy. Any recent changes?
oz: Yep I saw the same. DNS p95 shot to 150-300ms and some UDP retransmits on east-west. kube-dns and app logs show repeated retries.
infra-bot: [ALERT] coredns-0 latency > 200ms (3 restarts in 15m) — metric=coredns_latency_95 232ms
liam: Ran tcpdump on a couple affected nodes. Seeing lots of fragmented DNS UDP packets + ICMP 'frag needed' sometimes. Looks like MTU mismatch between overlay and underlying fabric when jumbo frames are enabled. Also sporadic drops on RDMA path when packets are >1500. Snippet:```17:05:12.345678 IP 10.0.4.12.53 > 10.0.2.45.33245: UDP, length 1280``` and then```ICMP frag-needed mtu 1400```
sana: Do we have a per-node DNS proxy/cache running? If cache misses escalate to coredns and packets get larger (EDNS/EDNS0), that could push into fragmentation land. We rolled a Corefile change earlier that enabled edns-payload and padding — could be increasing UDP size.
maya: We did a coredns config rollout at 10:04 UTC (bumped replicas to 3 and enabled EDNS padding). Timing lines up.
oz: For immediate mitigation I'll scale coredns up to 6 replicas and add `policy round_robin` + force TCP fallback for large responses in the Corefile. Also planning to apply an MSS clamp at the node level.
liam: Agreed. Quick kernel tweak we can push: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc=1` to avoid PMTU blackhole + iptables clamp-mss in CNI chain. That stops fragments for TCP; for UDP we need to ensure responses fit MTU or use TCP.
maya: I'm applying a DaemonSet to set clamp-mss and the sysctl on the gpu node-pool now. Also rolling the coredns config back to previous padding off as a test.
oz: Adding a temporary tcp-based forwarder for service discovery (udp->tcp) as a fallback so pod lookups don't blow up while we stabilize.
infra-bot: Action log — daemonset/clamp-mss applied at 10:30 UTC, coredns scaled to 6 at 10:31 UTC, corefile reverted at 10:33 UTC.
maya: After clamp + revert, p95 DNS latency down to ~18ms and pod lookup errors dropped to ~0.5%. Autoscaler warns cleared.
liam: We'll follow up with a postmortem on root cause — likely multi-factor: EDNS padding change + region fabric MTU config mismatch + RDMA path sensitivity. Recommend: enforce cluster MTU policy, add CI check for Corefile changes that increase UDP payloads, and implement TCP fallback in Corefile by default.
sana: Also worth testing different RDMA configs on a staging node-pool; jumbo frames should be coordinated across the whole stack.
maya: Thanks all — keeping this thread open for 15m to verify no regressions. :thumbsup:
